pages.text: A propeller pushes air and the ship pushes back. A Propeller Bearing spins a structure of sails. Any structure with at least two sail-like blocks counts, and more sails give more thrust.

pages.title: Propeller Bearing
pages.text: Attaches to the block in front. Reversing rotation reverses thrust; a wrench does too. Goggles show thrust and airflow.

pages.title: Gyroscopic Propeller Bearing
pages.text: Keeps its propeller upright, for helicopters. Facing down it steadies top-heavy ships. Redstone resets the tilt.

pages.title: Smart Propeller
pages.text: Makes thrust when spun and tilts along one axis to try to face upward. A wrench reverses its thrust.

pages.title: Wooden Propeller
pages.text: A ready-made small propeller. The Andesite Propeller is its sturdier twin.
A propeller already moving through air pushes less, because the air is moving too. Thrust also fades with altitude, and props are of little use where there is no air.
pages.title: Limits
Symmetric Sail
pages.text: Only makes drag, never lift. Angle it for turning or stabilising. Also handy for windmills; it needs no glue.
